Runtime consumption is `java.text.MessageFormat` (with embedded `ChoiceFormat`) on the template `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` :

* `{0}=inputHint` (attribute name), `{1}=min`, `{2}=max` supplied by `MultiValueValidator`. `MessageFormat` evaluates the 4th argument `{2,choice,...}` against `max` (arg 2): `0#values` → `max==0` → `values`, `1#value` → `max==1` → `value`, `1<values` → `max>1` → `values`. Result e.g. `Attribute foo must have at least 1 and at most 1 value` vs `... at most 2 values`.

Rendering contexts where `new MessageFormat(value,locale).format(args)` is invoked:

* **Server-side FreeMarker theme rendering** – `MessageFormatterMethod.exec()` exposes FreeMarker method `msg` used in login/account/admin `.ftl` pages (registration, account update, etc.). Same for `AdvancedMessageFormatterMethod`.
* **Admin REST JSON error response** – `UsersResource.createUser()` (and `UserResource.validateUserProfile` path) does `MessageFormat.format(messages.getProperty(e.getMessage()), e.getParameters())` and throws `ErrorResponseException(BAD_REQUEST)` whose JSON `errorMessage` is shown as inline/toast error in the React Admin-UI / Account-UI.

Build-time `VerifyMessageProperties` strips `{n,choice,...}` to `...` only for OWASP HTML sanitizer check, not runtime.

cenario.answer:
Derived `englishFile` at `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` lines 74-75 is `file.getAbsolutePath()` with two regex `replaceAll` transformations applied in sequence:

1. `replaceAll("resources-community","resources")` takes the absolute path string and replaces every regex-match of the literal substring `resources-community` (no metacharacters, `-` literal outside `[]`) with `resources`. For a path containing a `resources-community` directory segment e.g. `.../resources-community/.../messages_pt_BR.properties` it produces `.../resources/.../messages_pt_BR.properties`.

2. Chained `.replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties","_en.properties")` treats first argument as regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` : literal `_` then `*` (0+ greedy) of character class `[a-zA-Z-_]` (`a-z`, `A-Z`, literal `-`/`_` - with `Z-_` being range `Z`(90) to `_`(95) in Java regex, thus also `[ \ ] ^` but intended to allow letters/`-`/`_`), then literal `.properties` (`\.` escaped dot). It matches the suffix substring from the locale `_` to the end `.properties` and replaces each match with `_en.properties`. For `.../messages_pt_BR.properties` it matches `_pt_BR.properties`; for `.../messages_zh_CN.properties` it matches `_zh_CN.properties`; for hyphen variant `_pt-BR` style it matches the hyphen as well because `-` is in class. Greedy `*` makes it match longest from first `_` to `.properties` (e.g. `_pt_BR.properties` whole suffix). The resulting `englishFile` string is therefore the community-path normalized to `resources` and locale suffix normalized to `_en.properties`, e.g. `.../resources/theme/messages_en.properties`.

At `misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:75` the regex is `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` used via `String.replaceAll` to map `…_[locale].properties` -> `…_en.properties`.

Inside Java `java.util.regex` (used by `String.replaceAll`/`Pattern`) a `-` inside `[]` is a **range operator** when it appears between two characters (not at start/end and not escaped `\-`). In `[a-zA-Z-_]` the structure is `a-z` + `A-Z` + `Z-_` :

* `a-z` = U+0061-007A
* `A-Z` = U+0041-005A  
* `Z-_` = U+005A(90) to U+005F(95) = `Z [ \ ] ^ _`

Therefore `-` is **consumed as the operator**, not a member. The class does **NOT** contain literal `-` (U+002D). It is equivalent to `[a-zA-ZZ-_]` / `[A-Za-z\[\\\]^_]*` = `a-z` + `A-Z` + `[ \ ] ^ _` ( `_` and `Z` already covered). `*` is 0 or more, so it matches the empty string and any length string consisting solely of that set (inadvertently allowing `[ \ ] ^` and failing to match intended literal `-`). Intended literal hyphen would be `[a-zA-Z_-]` or `[a-zA-Z\-_]`.

In normal `theme-verifier` execution neither `FileInputStream` should throw `IOException`, but the code defensively wraps each in `RuntimeException`; `verify()` also wraps `Files.readString` `IOException` in `MojoExecutionException`. Only two logical callers exist: `ThemeVerifierMojo.execute()` (production Mojo) and `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest` (tests). Mojo propagates both `MojoExecutionException` and unchecked `RuntimeException` to Maven; tests propagate `MojoExecutionException` via `throws` and let `RuntimeException` fail the test.

* `englishFile` stream is derived via string replacements from `file.getAbsolutePath()` at 74-75. In normal themes every locale file has a corresponding `_en.properties` (and `resources-community` -> `resources` mapping), so file exists and no `IOException`. If derivation fails or English file missing, `FileInputStream(englishFile)` at 76 throws `FileNotFoundException` -> `RuntimeException` at 79, aborting the mojo with unchecked exception rather than `MojoExecutionException`/`MojoFailureException`.

Callers:
* `ThemeVerifierMojo:51` iterates files from `FileUtils.iterateFiles` and calls `new VerifyMessageProperties(file).verify()` with no local try/catch; `execute()` at 42 declares `throws MojoExecutionException, MojoFailureException`, so `MojoExecutionException` from `Files.readString` propagates directly to Maven, and `RuntimeException` from either `FileInputStream` propagates unchecked (Maven wraps as build error). * `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest:32,38,44,50` each call `getFile(...).verify()` and declare `throws MojoExecutionException`, with no catch for `RuntimeException` - test fails on either exception.

cegos.answer:
Strings reaching diff at 99-111 via `verifySafeHtml` (65-114):

* `value` is not raw bundle value: `bundle.getString(key)` -> `normalizeValue` -> `santizeAnchors(key,value,englishValue)`. `englishValue` is similarly normalized and used for policy decision and anchor allow-list.
* `sanitized` is `policy.sanitize(value)` where `policy = containsHtml(englishValue) ? POLICY_SOME_HTML : POLICY_NO_HTML` then `unescapeHtml4(sanitized)` then `replace("<!-- -->","")`.
* Length: no invariant enforced. Guard is only `!Objects.equals(sanitized,value)`. Sanitizer with `POLICY_NO_HTML` (empty allow-list) typically shortens (`sanitized.length < value.length`) by stripping tags; with `POLICY_SOME_HTML` (allows br,p,strong,b) may be equal length if only allowed tags, or shorter if disallowed tags/attributes stripped; replacement/removal of `<!-- -->` also shortens; `unescapeHtml4` neutralizes escaping so can restore/expand but net typically `sanitized.length <= value.length`. Equal-length-different-content possible (e.g., attribute stripping/replacement). Code handles any `<,=,>` via `min(sanitized.length,value.length)` bounds but not `start+end < length`.
* Prefix/suffix: `start` = longest common prefix bounded by `minLen`; `end` = longest common suffix bounded by `minLen`, computed independently after prefix. No overlap guard (`start+end` may exceed `minLen`). Then reported via `value.substring(start,value.length-end)` and `sanitized.substring(start,sanitized.length-end)`. If `start+end > length` substring throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` (e.g., sanitized much longer or strings share overlapping prefix+suffix).
